The model calls that a *continuation* with no steps of its own, so the subject check on the supersede path never sees it — before the fix the run kept General Medicine and re-proposed its slots, and every reworded clarification did the same thing, because each one was another continuation. `same_run: false` is the whole assertion: the eye request must not be answered by the run that routed elsewhere.

name: a-selection-lands-at-in-progress
pins: Round 6 item 1, and the worst of the session. A run at in_progress that had shown times could not hear an answer to them: the model called the reply a new request, the mapping correctly refused to supersede a run with itself, and the refusal answers with more times. Seven consecutive messages to one run each drew the identical availability list. Graded on the state machine, not the wording � a selection must leave the run holding a slot and waiting, on the run it started on.

name: a-booking-selection-is-not-a-new-request
pins: Round 6 item 4. 'Lets book the 10am slot' was classified conflicting with steps [route, cancel] � a cancel plan for a message that says book, residue from two earlier cancel attempts in the history � and the supersede path built the replacement run from those steps unchecked. The run routed to General Medicine with low confidence and died in a staff queue. The message names a time the run had just offered, so it is a selection and never reaches classification at all.

name: cancelling-is-not-routed-to-a-department
pins: Round 6 item 2. 'I want to cancel my appointment' was planned as [route, cancel] twice in one session; routing found no department words in a sentence that contains none, dropped to low confidence, and both runs stopped in front of staff for a patient who had a working cancel path. The department is a fact about the appointment being cancelled, never a question about the request, so validate_plan strips the routing step a model names anyway.

turns.message: I want to cancel my appointment

name: a-scare-does-not-consume-a-queued-request
pins: Round 6 item 5. An unrelated safety trigger arriving over a run that was waiting for staff escalated *that* run � and escalated is terminal, so the queued ambiguous-routing request died without a human ever deciding it, while the surviving queue item's reason still described a department choice. The scare is not that request, so it gets a run of its own and the queue keeps both.

name: an-affirmative-is-never-read-as-a-decline
pins: Round 10 item 1. At pending_confirmation holding a 2:00 PM slot, 'yes lets confirm it' came back from the model as verdict=decline with the affirmative sentence quoted in its own reason field, and code applied it unread: the proposal was cleared and the patient was told nothing had been booked. A decline clears a held time, so it needs a decline cue — and a word of agreement vetoes one whatever sits beside it. Note that under the mock this conversation proves little: the understudy reads that sentence as a non-answer, so the guard is never reached. It is a live probe, and the guard itself is pinned with a scripted provider in tests/unit/test_confirmation_flow.py.
